trust_decision.summary: assertSecureUrl decides whether a URL may be fetched; any URL starting with 'data:' is accepted before parsing, with no size limit (PT-005).

landing_point.why: The advisory names the data: early-return in assertSecureUrl, and it is the only data: check in core/src.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API secureFetch()/assertSecureUrl(), and through them restClient, graphqlClient, protobufClient, exportToEndpoint, FeatureFlagProvider url

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None useful: every fetch route calls the same assertSecureUrl, so a single-line length cap covers them all and no route can be left open.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: data: URLs below the cap must still be allowed (the existing test expects a small base64 data: URL to pass); relative and https URLs follow the same function.

O6_input_shapes: string URL starting with 'data:' longer than 1 MiB (the length check sits on the string that secureFetch derives from a string, URL or Request input, core/src/shared/secure-fetch.ts:71)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an exporter variant (e.g. sendBeacon-based) that does its own scheme allowlist with a data: early-return instead of calling assertSecureUrl
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pentest report's attack surface lists telemetry navigator.sendBeacon (fix.diff:43), and telemetry export is a separate package path where a maintainer might inline a lighter check.

O9_family: resource exhaustion via unbounded data: URI accepted by a URL allowlist (filed as CWE-918)

O10_build.toolchain: bun (bun test with nogginlessdom preload), node >=24, tsc

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (url.length > LIMIT) throw` inside the data: branch of assertSecureUrl, which is also the full and correct fix.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit also bundles PT-001 (throw on URL parse failure), PT-002 (gql metacharacters), PT-003 (CSS sanitization in render-to-string), PT-004 (redirect: 'error') and PT-008 (loopback list); these belong to other advisories.

PT-004's redirect default is applied only in secureFetch (fix.diff:466); rest.ts:188, graphql.ts:111, protobuf.ts:358 and metrics.ts:346 call fetch directly without it. This is a different advisory and was not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size tool used).

O1 counts the callers of assertSecureUrl/secureFetch in core/src (core/src/features/feature-flags.ts:68, core/src/client/rest.ts:187, core/src/client/graphql.ts:110, core/src/client/protobuf.ts:357, core/src/telemetry/metrics.ts:345, plus direct secureFetch); components/ and site/ were only searched for raw fetch( calls.

Whether a case variant such as 'DATA:' is rejected relies on WHATWG URL parsing (protocol 'data:', not https, empty hostname leads to the throw at core/src/shared/secure-fetch.ts:58); this was not executed.
The fix diff adds no test files, so the regression_tests_in_pinned_commit check does not apply.
